title: Bekhorot 19
description: The close of chapter two, on an animal born by caesarean section and the one that follows it, and the baraita on what makes a firstborn; and the opening of chapter three, on an animal bought from a gentile when no one knows whether it has given birth, and which majorities the Rabbis follow.
topics: 🔪 Born by caesarean section and the one that follows it: Rabbi Tarfon’s doubt, Rabbi Akiva’s “neither”
📜 “Firstborn”, “male”, “that which opens the womb”: a generalization that needs a detail and a detail that needs a generalization
❓ Is a firstborn in one aspect a firstborn? Rav Sherevya, Abaye and Ravina
⚖️ Rav Aḥa of Difti’s case of a female born by caesarean section settles it like Abaye
📖 Chapter 3 opens: an animal bought from a gentile, and Rabbi Yishmael’s ages for goat, ewe, cow and donkey
🩸 Rabbi Akiva: a murky discharge, an afterbirth or a fetal sac also exempts
🏪 Nine stores and the Sanhedrin: an evident majority, and the male and female minor

a1.he: דְּהָךְ דְּלָא בִּיכְּרָה שְׁבִיחַ טְפֵי צְרִיכָא.

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן וְהַבָּא אַחֲרָיו, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶם יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ, וְיֵאָכְלוּ בְּמוּמָן לַבְּעָלִים. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶן אֵינָן בְּכוֹר, הָרִאשׁוֹן — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינוֹ ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״, וְהַשֵּׁנִי — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקְּדָמוֹ אַחֵר.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ: בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד, אִי הָוֵי בְּכוֹר אִי לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ: בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר.

a4.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִכְּלָל הַצָּרִיךְ לִפְרָט וּמִפְּרָט הַצָּרִיךְ לִכְלָל, כֵּיצַד? ״קַדֶּשׁ לִי כׇל בְּכוֹר״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ נְקֵבָה בַּמַּשְׁמָע? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״זָכָר״.

a5.he: אִי ״זָכָר״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצְתָה נְקֵבָה לְפָנָיו? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״. אִי ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יָצָא אַחַר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּכוֹר״.

a6.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא לְאַבָּיֵי: רֵישָׁא לָא קָנָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא ״בְּכוֹר״, אַלְמָא בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר. סֵיפָא קָנָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא ״בְּכוֹר״, אַלְמָא בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר!

a7.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, וְרֵישָׁא הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִי זָכָר, יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״.

a8.he: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, וְסֵיפָא הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ יָצָא אַחֵר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן קָדוֹשׁ, ״בְּכוֹר״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי?

b1.he: אִי לְמַעוֹטֵי הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה לְפָנָיו — מִ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״ נָפְקָא! אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ ״בְּכוֹר״ לְמַעוֹטֵי הֵיכָא דְּיוֹצֵא אַחַר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן.

b2.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר, תִּינַח הֵיכָא דְּיָצָא זָכָר יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן וְזָכָר דֶּרֶךְ רֶחֶם, דְּלָא קָדוֹשׁ, דְּאִימַּעוּט לֵידָה מִ״בְּכוֹר״, דִּבְכוֹר לִרְחָמִים אִיכָּא, בְּכוֹר לִזְכָרִים לֵיכָּא.

b3.he: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה דֶּרֶךְ דּוֹפֶן וְזָכָר דֶּרֶךְ רֶחֶם — לִיקְדַּשׁ, דְּהָא אִיכָּא בְּכוֹר לִזְכָרִים וּבְכוֹר לְרֶחֶם! אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְאַבָּיֵי.

b5.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מִן הַגּוֹי, וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם בִּיכְּרָה אִם לֹא בִּיכְּרָה. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: עֵז בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ — וַדַּאי לַכֹּהֵן, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — סָפֵק. רָחֵל בַּת שְׁתַּיִם — וַדַּאי לַכֹּהֵן, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — סָפֵק. פָּרָה וַחֲמוֹר בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ — וַדַּאי לַכֹּהֵן, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — סָפֵק.

b6.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִילּוּ בְּוָולָד בִּלְבַד הַבְּהֵמָה נִפְטֶרֶת כִּדְבָרֶיךָ, אֶלָּא אָמְרוּ: סִימָן הַוָּולָד בִּבְהֵמָה דַּקָּה — טִינּוּף, וּבַגַּסָּה — שִׁילְיָא, וּבָאִשָּׁה — שָׁפִיר וְשִׁילְיָא.

b7.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁבִּיכְּרָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם, וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה — הֲרֵי זֶה לַכֹּהֵן, וְאִם סָפֵק — יֵאָכֵל בְּמוּמוֹ לַבְּעָלִים.

b8.he: גְּמָ׳ מִיכָּן וְאֵילָךְ, אַמַּאי סָפֵק? הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב בְּהֵמוֹת, וְרוֹב בְּהֵמוֹת מִתְעַבְּרוֹת וְיוֹלְדוֹת בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתָן נִינְהוּ, וְהָא וַדַּאי מֵילָד אוֹלֵיד! לֵימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא?

b9.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, כִּי אָזְלִי בָּתַר רוּבָּא בְּרוּבָּא דְּאִיתֵיהּ קַמַּן, כְּגוֹן תֵּשַׁע חֲנוּיוֹת וְסַנְהֶדְרִין, אֲבָל רוּבָּא דְּלֵיתֵיהּ קַמַּן — לָא אָזְלִי רַבָּנַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא.

b10.he: וְהָא קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה, דְּרוּבָּא דְּלֵיתֵיהּ קַמַּן, וְקָאָזְלִי רַבָּנַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא, דִּתְנַן: קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה לֹא חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: יָפֶה אָמַרְתָּ שֶׁאֵין חוֹלְצִין, ״אִישׁ״ כָּתוּב בַּפָּרָשָׁה, וּמַקְּשִׁינַן אִשָּׁה לְאִישׁ.

b11.he: מָה טַעַם אֵין מְיַיבְּמִין? אָמַר לָהֶם: קָטָן — שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא סָרִיס, קְטַנָּה — שֶׁמָּא תִּמָּצֵא אַיְילוֹנִית, וְנִמְצְאוּ פּוֹגְעִין בְּעֶרְוָה.

b12.he: וְרַבָּנַן, זִיל בָּתַר רוּבָּא קְטַנִּים, וְרוֹב קְטַנִּים לָאו סָרִיסִים נִינְהוּ; זִיל בָּתַר קְטַנּוֹת, וְרוֹב קְטַנּוֹת לָאו אַיְילוֹנִית נִינְהוּ!

messages.text: Continued from 18b: the Gemara is explaining why the mishna needed all three cases in which Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva disagree. Had it taught only the case of two ewes that had not given birth, one might say that where one ewe had given birth and one had not, and they bore two males, Rabbi Akiva concedes to Rabbi Tarfon…
…that this offspring born to the ewe that had not previously given birth is superior. Consequently, it was necessary to teach each case.

notes.he: והכי נמי בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ח:) מר זוטרא איקלע בי רב אשי חתכי לקמיה בשרא אמרו ליה לטעום מר דמברי משום דבוכרא הוא ועגלא תילתא לאו היינו שלישי לבטן כדפירש"י כדאמרינן סנהדרין (דף סה:) עבדי ליה עגלא תילתא אלא דתילתא לשון חשיבות כמו ושלישים על כולו (שמות י״ד:ז׳):
notes.en: That this one that had not given birth is superior: so too in the first chapter of Temura (8b): Mar Zutra visited the house of Rav Ashi. They cut meat before him [and] said to him: Let the Master taste, for it is choice, since it is a firstborn. And “egla tilta” [the “third” calf] does not mean, as Rashi explained, the third of its mother’s womb, as we say in Sanhedrin (65b), “They would prepare for themselves an egla tilta”; rather, “tilta” is a term of importance, as in “and officers [shalishim] over all of them” (Exodus 14:7).

messages.text: Mishna
With regard to an animal born by caesarean section and the offspring that follows it, since there is uncertainty whether each is a firstborn, neither is given to the priest.

notes.he: בכור שיצא דרך דופן הבא אחריו בכור (לזכרים ולא) לרחמים ולא ללידה שכבר יצא אחר קודם לו:
notes.en: Mishna. Born by caesarean section [yotzei dofen]: a firstborn that emerged through the side. The one that comes after it is a firstborn (for males and not) for the womb, and not for birth, since another one already emerged before it. [The words in parentheses are bracketed in the printed text.]

notes.he: יוצא דופן שלא יצא דרך הרחם ממש אלא כגון שקרעוהו ויצא מן הצד או כדאמרינן בבהמה המקשה שנגממו כתלי בית הרחם והדר יצא:
notes.en: Born by caesarean section: that did not emerge through the womb itself, but, for example, they cut [the mother] open and it emerged from the side; or as we say in [the chapter] Behema HaMaksha, that the walls of the womb were cut away and then it emerged.

notes.he: דרך הרחם כגון שחזר והבריא הרחם והיה בקודם גמום ואחר יצא זה מרחם (גמום) שלם:
notes.en: And the one that comes after it: through the womb; for example, the womb healed again. It had been cut before, and afterward this one emerged from a whole womb.

messages.text: Both of them must graze until they become unfit, and they may be eaten in their blemished state by their owner.

notes.he: דספק בכור הן דמספקא לר' טרפון בכור לדבר אחד אי הוי בכור אי לא הוי בכור:
notes.en: Both of them must graze etc.: since they are uncertain firstborns, for Rabbi Tarfon is uncertain whether one that is a firstborn in one aspect is a firstborn or is not a firstborn.

notes.he: משום דיוצא דופן הוי בכור ללידה. והבא אחריו הוי בכור לרחמים. רבי עקיבא אמר שניהם כו':
notes.en: Both of them must graze etc.: because the one born by caesarean section is a firstborn for birth, and the one that comes after it is a firstborn for the womb. Rabbi Akiva says: Neither of them etc.

messages.text: Neither of them is firstborn; the first because it is not the one that opens the womb (see Exodus 13:12), as this animal did not itself open the womb, and the second because the other one preceded it.

verse.he: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כׇל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר ׀ שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: you shall set apart for GOD every first issue of the womb: every male firstling that your cattle drop shall be GOD’s.

messages.text: Gemara
With regard to what do Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Tarfon disagree?
messages.quote: Both of them must graze until they become unfit

messages.text: Rabbi Tarfon is uncertain with regard to an animal that is a firstborn in one aspect, e.g., first to be born or first to open the womb, whether it is considered a firstborn or whether it is not considered a firstborn. And conversely, it is obvious to Rabbi Akiva that an animal which is a firstborn in only one aspect is not considered a firstborn.

notes.he: או ללידה או לרחמים הוי בכור ואע"ג דלא הוי לכל מילי בכור. דלתלת מילי צריך למיהוי בכור ללידה ולרחמים ולזכרים רבי עקיבא פשיטא ליה דבכור לדבר אחד. כלומר דאי חסר אחד מהני תלת לא הוי בכור:
notes.en: A firstborn in one aspect: it is a firstborn either for birth or for the womb, even though it is not a firstborn in every respect. For in three things it must be a firstborn: for birth, for the womb and for males. To Rabbi Akiva it is obvious [that] a firstborn in one aspect [is not a firstborn]; that is, if it lacks one of these three, it is not a firstborn.

messages.text: With regard to the definition of a firstborn, the Sages taught in a baraita:
This halakha can be derived by means of the form of exegesis known as: From a generalization that requires a detail, and from a detail that requires a generalization. How so?

notes.he: שהכלל צריך שיהא הפרט עמו:
notes.en: Gemara. From a generalization that requires a detail: the generalization needs the detail to be with it.

notes.he: יש שהפרט צריך שיהא הכלל עמו:
notes.en: From a detail that requires a generalization: there is [a case] where the detail needs the generalization to be with it.

notes.he: פי' בקונט' שזהו כלל ופרט דבכור כלל זכר פרט ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט והך רישא לאו פירושא דכלל צריך לפרט הוא אלא מציעתא וסיפא דקתני אי זכר יכול אפי' יצתה נקבה לפניו ת"ל פטר רחם וזה לא פטר תחלת רחם והיינו כלל הצריך לפרט שאין אתה יכול להבין מה הכלל אומר עד שיבוא הפרט ופירשו לפי שיש לפרש בכור לכמה צדדין בכור לכל הוולדות או בכור לרחמים אע"פ שאינו בכור לוולדות כגון שיצא דרך רחם אחר יוצא דופן או בכור לזכרים אע"פ שיצתה נקבה לפניו דרך רחם בא הפרט ופירש שאינו קרוי בכור אא"כ הוא בכור לרחמים שפטר ופתח את הרחם וכיוצא בזו שנינו בפ' כסוי הדם (חולין פח:) אצל וכסהו בעפר יכול יכסהו באבן או יכפה עליו הכלי ת"ל בעפר אין לי אלא עפר מנין לרבות חרסית ונעורת של פשתן כו' ת"ל וכסהו ומקשינן ואימא וכסהו כלל בעפר פרט כלל ופרט אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט ומשנינן משום דהוה ליה כלל הצריך לפרט ואין דנין אותו בכלל ופרט לפי שיש לפרש כסוי בשני דרכים אחד בדבר הגס כגון אבן או כלי ואחד בדבר הדק לכך כתב בעפר ופירש וכסהו בדבר דק הנבלל בו ומכסהו הכתוב מדבר ע"כ לשון הקונטרס והשתא פירושו יתכן לפי דברי רבינא דבסמוך דאמר בכור לדבר אחד הוי בכור אבל במסקנא דשמעתין אמרי' דמחוורתא כאביי דאמר בכור לדבר אחד לא הוי בכור ולאביי לא הוי כלל צריך לפרט לכל דבר דאי אפשר לפרש בכור אלא לצד אחד ומיהו יש לפרש לאביי דאי לאו פרט הוה אמינא דאפי' יוצא דופן הוא בכור כיון דהוי בכור לוולדות ואע"ג דלא הוי בכור לרחמים ור"י מפרש לאביי בכור ופטר רחם תרווייהו כלל ותרווייהו פרט ותרווייהו צריכי להדדי ובכל אחד אתה מוצא כלל הצריך לפרט ופרט צריך לכלל שכל אחד סותם דבר אחד ומפרש דבר אחד דבכור משמע אפי' יוצא דופן ופטר רחם ממעיט ליה ופטר רחם משמע אפי' יצא אחר יוצא דופן ובכור ממעיט ליה ור"ת מפרש דבין הכא ובין בחולין (שם) הוי בכלל ופרט גמור דבעלמא דבכור משמע בין הכי ובין הכי ואתיא פרטא למעוטי וכן וכסהו משמע בין כסוי כלי בין כסוי עפר מה שירצה ופרטא משמע עפר דוקא ומה שתלמודא חשבו שם כלל הצריך לפרט לאו אכפיית הכלי דההיא ברייתא קאי אלא אדרשא אחריתי דדריש התם בריש פירקין (דף פג:) מבי"ת דבעפר דצריך שיתן עפר מלמטה ועפר מלמעלה דמוכסהו לא שמעי' למטה אלא למעלה ולא משום הפרט חושב שם כלל הצריך לפרט אלא משום ייתורא דבי"ת דכתיבא בפרט ובהך שמעתין לפרושי פרט הצריך לכלל קא אתא כדקתני בסיפא אי פטר רחם יכול אפי' יצא אחר יוצא דופן ת"ל בכור כדפי' בקונטרס ואע"ג דקתני מכלל הצריך לפרט ומפרט הצריך לכלל כיצד דמשמע דאתא נמי לפרושי כלל הצריך לפרט עיקר מילתא לא נקטיה אלא משום פרט הצריך לכלל:
notes.en: In brief: “How so? Sanctify to Me all the firstborn.” Rashi explained that this is a generalization and a detail: “firstborn” is the generalization, “male” the detail, and the generalization includes only what is in the detail. This first clause is not the explanation of “a generalization that requires a detail”; the middle and last clauses are: “If ‘male’, one might think even if a female emerged before it; the verse states: ‘that which opens the womb’,” and this one did not open the womb first. That is a generalization that requires a detail, since you cannot understand what the generalization says until the detail explains it, for “firstborn” can be read several ways: first of all the offspring; first for the womb though not first of the offspring (one that came through the womb after one born by caesarean section); or first of the males though a female preceded it through the womb. The detail explains that it is called a firstborn only if it is first for the womb, having opened the womb. Similarly in Kisui HaDam (Ḥullin 88b), on “and cover it with earth”: one might think he may cover it with a stone or overturn a vessel on it; the verse states “with earth.” [The Gemara there] asks: say “and cover it” is a generalization and “with earth” a detail, so the generalization includes only the detail; and answers that it is a generalization that requires a detail, which is not judged as a generalization and detail, since covering can be done two ways, with something coarse such as a stone or a vessel, or with something fine, so “with earth” was written to explain that the verse speaks of covering with something fine that mixes with [the blood]. [So far Rashi.] Tosafot: Rashi’s explanation fits Ravina below, who says a firstborn in one aspect is a firstborn. But the conclusion of our passage is that it is clear as Abaye, that a firstborn in one aspect is not a firstborn, and for Abaye it is not a generalization that requires a detail at all, since “firstborn” can be explained only one way. One could explain for Abaye that without the detail I would have said that even one born by caesarean section is a firstborn, since it is first of the offspring though not first for the womb. The Ri explains for Abaye: “firstborn” and “that which opens the womb” are each both a generalization and a detail, and each needs the other; each leaves one thing unspecified and specifies one: “firstborn” implies even one born by caesarean section, and “that which opens the womb” excludes it; “that which opens the womb” implies even one that came after one born by caesarean section, and “firstborn” excludes it. Rabbeinu Tam explains that both here and in Ḥullin it is a full generalization and detail: “firstborn” in general means either way and the detail comes to restrict it; “and cover it” means covering with a vessel or with earth, as one wishes, and the detail means earth specifically. What the Gemara there counts as a generalization that requires a detail does not refer to overturning the vessel in that baraita, but to another exposition at the beginning of that chapter (Ḥullin 83b), from the letter bet of “with earth” [ba’afar]: one must put earth below and earth above, for from “and cover it” we understand only above, not below; it is counted a generalization that requires a detail because of the extra bet in the detail, not because of the detail itself. And in our passage [the baraita] comes to explain a detail that requires a generalization, as the last clause teaches: “If ‘that which opens the womb’, one might think even one that emerged after one born by caesarean section; the verse states ‘firstborn’,” as Rashi explained. And although it teaches “from a generalization that requires a detail and from a detail that requires a generalization; how so?”, implying that it also comes to explain a generalization that requires a detail, it mentioned that only in passing; the main point is a detail that requires a generalization. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: The verse states: “Sanctify to Me all the firstborn, that which opens any womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of animal, it is Mine.” Had the verse written only the generalization: “Sanctify to Me all the firstborn,” one might have thought that even a female animal is included in the category of a firstborn.

verse.he: קַדֶּשׁ־לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר פֶּטֶר כׇּל־רֶחֶם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה לִי הוּא׃
verse.en: “Consecrate to Me every male first-born; human and animal, the first [male] issue of every womb among the Israelites is Mine.”

notes.he: הך רישא לאו פירושא דכלל הצריך לפרט הוא אלא מציעתא וסיפא:
notes.en: How so? Sanctify to Me etc.: this first clause is not an explanation of “a generalization that requires a detail”; rather the middle clause and the last clause are.

notes.he: היינו כלל דמשמע כל בכור או זכר או נקבה ת"ל זכר דהיינו פרט למעוטי נקבה:
notes.en: All the firstborn: this is the generalization, which implies every firstborn, male or female. The verse states “male,” which is the detail, to exclude a female.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states the detail: “Every firstborn male…you shall sanctify to the Lord.”

verse.he: כׇּל־הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verse.en: You shall consecrate to the ETERNAL your God all male firstlings that are born in your herd and in your flock: you must not work your firstling ox or shear your firstling sheep.

notes.he: כלל אפי' נקבות ת"ל זכר אשר יולד בבקרך ובצאנך הזכר זהו כלל ופרט השנוי במדה ראשונה של שלש עשרה מדות שהפרט בא למעט את הכלל ממשמעו ולהעמידו על הפרט ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט שהרי זה דומה לכלל ופרט השנוי אצל מדה ראשונה מן הבהמה כלל מן הבקר ומן הצאן פרט אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט:
notes.en: “All the firstborn”: a generalization, even females. The verse states “male”: “every firstborn that is born in your herd and in your flock, the male” (Deuteronomy 15:19). This is the generalization and detail taught in the first of the thirteen principles [of exegesis], where the detail comes to restrict the generalization from its plain meaning and confine it to the detail, and the generalization includes only what is in the detail. For this resembles the generalization and detail taught with the first principle: “of the animals” is a generalization, “of the herd and of the flock” is a detail; the generalization includes only what is in the detail.

messages.text: And had the verse stated only: “Every firstborn male,” one might have thought that the first male offspring of an animal has firstborn status, even in a case where a female emerged from the womb before it. Therefore, the verse states: “That which opens any womb,” to teach that only an animal that itself opens its mother’s womb can be a firstborn.

notes.he: בכור זכר יכול אפי' יצתה נקבה לפניו דרך רחם דהכי משמע בכור זכר בכור לזכרים שלא קדמו זכר אחר הוי בכור ואע"ג דאינו בכור ללידה ולרחמים:
notes.en: If [it said only] “firstborn male”: one might think even if a female emerged before it through the womb, for this is what “firstborn male” implies: a firstborn among males; since no other male preceded it, it is a firstborn, even though it is not a firstborn for birth or for the womb.

notes.he: איצטריך האי פרט לפרושי דלא מיקרי בכור עד דהוי בכור לרחמים משום דלא הוה ידעינן מאי משמעותא דכללא. ולא דמי לכלל ופרט דאהני פרט למעוטי כללא ולא לפרושי משמעותא כגון רישא דברייתא בכור יכול אפי' נקבה ת"ל זכר היינו כלל ופרט גמור דלא איצטריך לפרושי היכי דמי בכור דהא הנקבה בכור לכל מילי היא אלא למעוטי דלא תימא אף הנקבות קדושות בבכורה. ודכוותה בשחיטת חולין (דף פח:) וכסהו בעפר קרי ליה כלל הצריך לפרט משום דתרי גווני כסוי הוי כגון כפיית כלי עליו ועוד יש כסוי בדבר המתפזר כגון עפר וכיוצא בו לכך נאמר עפר למעוטי כסוי דבר שלם ולא דיינינן ליה בכלל ופרט גמור דנמעוט נמי שחיקת אבנים והגיר והזרניך:
notes.en: The verse states: “That which opens the womb”: this detail was needed to explain that it is not called a firstborn unless it is a firstborn for the womb, because we would not have known what the generalization meant. It is not like a generalization and a detail, where the detail serves to restrict the generalization and not to explain its meaning, such as the first clause of the baraita: “Firstborn: one might think even a female; the verse states: male.” That is a full generalization and detail, for [the detail] was not needed to explain what a firstborn is, since a female is a firstborn in every respect; rather it comes to restrict, lest you say that females too are sanctified as firstborn. Similarly in Sheḥitat Ḥullin (Ḥullin 88b), “and cover it with earth” is called a generalization that requires a detail, because there are two kinds of covering: such as overturning a vessel over it, and covering with something that scatters, such as earth and the like. Therefore “earth” is stated, to exclude covering with a whole object; and we do not judge it as a full generalization and detail, [for then] we would also exclude ground stones, plaster and arsenic.

notes.he: נקבה לפניו דרך רחם דאכתי הוי בכור לזכרים:
notes.en: One might think even if a female emerged before it through the womb: for it is still a firstborn for males.

notes.he: דבעינן נמי בכור לרחמים:
notes.en: The verse states: “That which opens the womb”: for we also require a firstborn for the womb.

messages.text: And had the verse stated only: “That which opens any womb,” one might have thought that even an animal that emerged from the womb after its older sibling was born by caesarean section is considered firstborn. Therefore, the verse states: “All the firstborn,” to teach that only the first offspring can be considered a firstborn.

notes.dh: יכול אפי' יצא אחר יצא דופן
notes.he: והוא יצא דרך רחם:
notes.en: One might think even if it emerged after one born by caesarean section: and it itself emerged through the womb.

notes.he: דמשמע בכור לכל מילי בעינן והיינו פרט הצריך לכלל דזכר ופטר רחם שהוא פרט צריכין לבכור שאילו לא נאמר בכור הייתי אומר אע"פ שאינו בכור יקדש. ורוב פרטות שבתורה אינן צריכין לכללות שעמהן כגון (ויקרא א׳:ב׳) מן הבקר ומן הצאן לא היו צריכין שיכתב מן הבהמה וכי יתן איש אל רעהו חמור [או שור] או שה (שמות כ״ב:ט׳) אינן צריכין לוכל בהמה אלא שבא להיות מוסיף על הפרט. כלל הצריך לפרט שאין אתה יכול להבין מהו אומר עד שיבוא הפרט לפרשו כגון בכור זכר יכול אפי' יצתה נקבה לפניו דבכור שהוא כלל לא ידענא בכור למאי קאמר אי לזכרים אע"ג דלא לרחמים כגון האי אי לרחמים ולא לזכרים כגון זכר שיצא פטר רחם אחר יוצא דופן אי נמי עד דהוי בכור לרחמים ולולדות:
notes.en: “Firstborn”: which implies that we require a firstborn in every respect. This is a detail that requires a generalization: “male” and “that which opens the womb,” which are a detail, need “firstborn,” for had “firstborn” not been stated, I would have said that even though it is not a firstborn it is sanctified. Most details in the Torah do not need the generalizations that accompany them; for example, “of the herd and of the flock” (Leviticus 1:2) did not need “of the animals” to be written, and “If a man gives his neighbor a donkey [or an ox] or a sheep” (Exodus 22:9) does not need “or any animal”; rather [the generalization] comes to add to the detail. A generalization that requires a detail: you cannot understand what it says until the detail comes and explains it. For example, “firstborn male: one might think even if a female emerged before it”: for “firstborn,” which is the generalization, I do not know in what sense it is said: whether for males even though not for the womb, as in this case; or for the womb and not for males, such as a male that opened the womb after one born by caesarean section; or else only when it is a firstborn both for the womb and for the offspring.

notes.he: היינו פרט וכלל דליכא למשמע מינה אלא לרחמים:
notes.en: If [only] “that which opens the womb”: this is a detail and a generalization, for from it one would understand only [a firstborn] for the womb.

notes.dh: יכול אפי' יצא אחר יוצא דופן נקבה ת"ל בכור
notes.he: דהיינו פרט [כלל] ולכל מילי בעינן בכור והאי לא הוי בכור ללידה:
notes.en: One might think even if it emerged after a female born by caesarean section; the verse states “firstborn”: which is the detail [emended: the generalization], and we require a firstborn in every respect, and this one is not a firstborn for birth.

messages.text: @Abaye In the first clause, the baraita does not cite proof from the word “firstborn” that a male born after a female is not considered a firstborn. Apparently, an animal that is a firstborn in one aspect is called a firstborn, otherwise the baraita would not have had to derive the exclusion of a male born after a female from the phrase “that which opens any womb”; it could have cited the word “firstborn.”
messages.quote: even in a case where a female emerged from the womb before it. Therefore, the verse states: “That which opens any womb,”

notes.dh: רישא לא נסיב לה תלמודא בכור
notes.he: מציעתא קרי רישא דקתני יכול אפי' יצתה נקבה לפניו ת"ל פטר רחם מדלא נסיב לה תלמודא ת"ל בכור דמשמע בכור לכל מילי אלמא לא מישתמע ליה דבכור לכל מילי משמע ולהכי לא נסביה דלא מימעוט האי מיניה דכיון דלא יצא זכר לפניו בכור קרינא דבכור לזכרים הוא אלמא ס"ל בכור דקרא בכור לדבר אחד הוא הוי משמע:
notes.en: In the first clause, the baraita does not cite “firstborn”: he calls the middle clause “the first clause,” which teaches: “One might think even if a female emerged before it; the verse states: that which opens the womb.” Since the baraita did not cite “the verse states: firstborn,” which would imply a firstborn in every respect, evidently it does not take [the word] to mean a firstborn in every respect; and that is why it did not cite it, since this case would not be excluded by it: since no male emerged before it, we call it a firstborn, for it is a firstborn for males. Evidently he holds that the “firstborn” of the verse means even a firstborn in one aspect.

notes.dh: רישא לא קנסיב ליה תלמודא בכור אלמא בכור לדבר אחד הוי בכור
notes.he: משמע דכיון דבכור לדבר אחד הוי בכור הוה מחייבינן אפי' יצתה נקבה לפניו אי לאו פטר רחם ותימה דרבי טרפון דמספקא ליה היה לו לחייב מספק כמו יוצא דופן ויוצא אחריו דלא ממעט יוצא דופן מפטר רחם וי"ל דנהי דלא מסתבר ליה למעוטי יוצא דופן מפטר רחם משום דהוי [בכלל וולדות] בין לזכרים בין לנקבות לכל הפחות אתא למעוטי היכא דיצתה נקבה לפניו דאי לאו הכי פטר רחם דכתב רחמנא למה לי:
notes.en: In the first clause the baraita does not cite “firstborn”; evidently a firstborn in one aspect is a firstborn: this implies that since a firstborn in one aspect is a firstborn, we would obligate even where a female emerged before it, were it not for “that which opens the womb.” And this is puzzling: Rabbi Tarfon, who is uncertain, should have obligated [that case] out of uncertainty, like one born by caesarean section and the one that follows it, since he does not exclude one born by caesarean section by “that which opens the womb.” One may answer: although he does not consider it reasonable to exclude one born by caesarean section by “that which opens the womb,” since it is [included among the offspring], whether of males or of females, at the least [the phrase] comes to exclude the case where a female emerged before it; for otherwise, why do I need “that which opens the womb” that the Merciful One wrote?

notes.dh: רישא לא קא נסיב לה בכור
notes.he: לכל מילי דהיינו רישא אי זכר וכו' ת"ל פטר רחם כלומר מדלא קאמר ת"ל בכור משמע דסבירא ליה דאע"ג דיצא אחר יוצא דופן נקבה הוי בכור הואיל והוי בכור לרחמים ולזכר אלמא דבכור לדבר אחד הוי בכור:
notes.en: In the first clause it does not cite “firstborn” [meaning] in every respect: this is the first clause, “If ‘male’ etc., the verse states: that which opens the womb.” That is, since it does not say “the verse states: firstborn,” it implies that it holds that even though it emerged after a female born by caesarean section, it is a firstborn, since it is a firstborn for the womb and for males. Evidently a firstborn in one aspect is a firstborn.

notes.he: ואע"ג דלתרין מילי הוי בכור כיון דמחוסר אחד קרי ליה בכור לדבר אחד:
notes.en: And even though it is a firstborn in two respects, since it lacks one, it is called a firstborn in one aspect.

messages.text: And in the last clause, the baraita does cite proof from the word “firstborn” that an animal whose older sibling was born by caesarean section is not considered a firstborn, despite the fact that it is a firstborn in one aspect. Apparently, a firstborn in one aspect is not called a firstborn. If so, the baraita is self-contradictory.
messages.quote: Therefore, the verse states: “All the firstborn,”

notes.he: אלמא בכור דכתב בקרא לכל מילי משמע דבכור לדבר אחד כגון האי דהוי בכור לרחמים (ולזכרים) אלא דלא הוי בכור לוולדות לא הוי בכור:
notes.en: And in the last clause the baraita does cite “firstborn”: evidently the “firstborn” written in the verse means in every respect, so that a firstborn in one aspect, such as this one, which is a firstborn for the womb (and for males) but not a firstborn for the offspring, is not a firstborn. [The words in parentheses are bracketed in the printed text.]

notes.he: היינו סיפא אי פטר רחם אלמא דלכל מילי בעי בכור. וקשיא רישא לסיפא:
notes.en: The last clause cites “firstborn”: this is the last clause, “If ‘that which opens the womb’”; evidently it requires a firstborn in every respect. And the first clause contradicts the last.

messages.text: @Rav Sherevya Actually, a firstborn in one aspect is not called a firstborn, and this is what the first clause is saying: Had the verse stated only: “Every firstborn male,” one might have thought that even an animal born by caesarean section is itself considered a firstborn. Therefore, the verse states: “That which opens any womb,” to teach that an animal must itself open the womb to be considered a firstborn.
messages.quote: In the first clause, the baraita does not cite proof from the word “firstborn”

notes.dh: לעולם בכור לדבר אחד לא הוי בכור
notes.he: כלומר דקרא לכל מילי משמע והאי דלא נסיב תלמודא בכור ברישא:
notes.en: Actually, a firstborn in one aspect is not a firstborn: that is, the verse means in every respect. And as for the baraita not citing “firstborn” in the first clause:

notes.dh: ה"ק אי זכר יכול אפי' יצא דרך דופן ת"ל פטר רחם
notes.he: דהשתא לא מצי תלמודא נסיב בכור למעוטי להאי דהא בכור לכל דבר הוא דהא לא קדמו אחר בעולם להכי נקט פטר רחם וממילא (נמי) אימעיט נמי יצתה נקבה לפניו מפטר רחם:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: If [only] “male,” one might think even if it emerged through the side; the verse states “that which opens the womb”: for here the baraita cannot cite “firstborn” to exclude it, since it is a firstborn in every respect, as no other preceded it in the world. That is why it took “that which opens the womb,” and as a matter of course the case where a female emerged before it is also excluded by “that which opens the womb.”

notes.he: ורישא תריץ הכי אי זכר יכול אפילו יצא דרך דופן הוא עצמו הבכור ת"ל פטר רחם וזה אינו פטר רחם. ועכשיו כיון דלא תני יכול אפילו יצאה נקבה לפניו דרך רחם ת"ל פטר רחם דדייקינן מינה הא יצאה נקבה לפניו דרך דופן דאפילו הכי הוי בכור אלא תני יכול אפילו יצא דרך דופן דליכא למידק מינה הא יצאה נקבה לפניו דרך דופן דלא קא מיירי בנקבה כלל ש"מ דבכור לכל מילי בעי כמו סיפא:
notes.en: Actually etc. And the first clause is to be explained thus: “If ‘male’, one might think even if it itself emerged through the side it is the firstborn; the verse states: that which opens the womb,” and this one did not open the womb. And now, since it does not teach “one might think even if a female emerged before it through the womb; the verse states: that which opens the womb,” from which we would infer that if a female emerged before it through the side it is a firstborn even so, but rather teaches “one might think even if it emerged through the side,” from which nothing can be inferred, since it does not speak of a female at all, [the printed text is corrupt here; an editor suggests: one may well say that we require a firstborn in every respect, as in the last clause] conclude from it that we require a firstborn in every respect, as in the last clause.

messages.text: The word “firstborn” cannot be cited as proof that an animal born by caesarean section is not a firstborn, as such an animal was in fact born first. Therefore, the tanna cites the phrase “that which opens any womb.” Once this phrase is cited, then a male born after a female is excluded as well, despite the fact that this halakha could have been derived from the word “firstborn.”

There is a different explanation: Actually, a firstborn in one aspect is called a firstborn, and the halakha is not derived from the meaning of the word “firstborn” itself, but from the fact that it is superfluous.

notes.dh: רבינא אמר בכור לדבר אחד הוי בכור
notes.he: כלומר [בכור] דקרא אפי' לדבר אחד משמע וסיפא דנסיב תלמודא בכור למעוטי יצא אחר יוצא דופן לא ממשמעות דקרא נפקא דקרא משמע בכור לדבר אחד אלא מריבויא דקרא:
notes.en: Ravina says: a firstborn in one aspect is a firstborn: that is, the [word] “firstborn” of the verse means even in one aspect. And as for the last clause, where the baraita cites “firstborn” to exclude one that emerged after one born by caesarean section: this is not derived from the meaning of the verse, for the verse means a firstborn [even] in one aspect, but from the extra word of the verse.

notes.dh: רבינא אמר לעולם בכור לדבר אחד
notes.he: דמחוסר לדבר אחד בלבד הוי בכור כדדייקינן מעיקרא ברישא:
notes.en: Ravina says: Actually, a firstborn in one aspect: one that lacks one thing only is a firstborn, as we inferred initially from the first clause.

messages.text: And this is what the last clause is saying: If it enters your mind that an animal which emerged from the womb after its older sibling was born by caesarean section is sanctified, why do I need the word “firstborn” that the Merciful One wrote?

notes.dh: דאי ס"ד כו' בכור דכתב רחמנא
notes.he: דמשמע שיהא בכור במקצת למה לי לכתוב פטר רחם זכר תקדיש ולישתוק:
notes.en: For if it enters your mind etc., “firstborn” that the Merciful One wrote: which implies that it is a firstborn in part; why do I need it? Let it write “that which opens the womb… the male, you shall sanctify,” and be silent.

notes.he: דמשמע לך דלכל מילי בעי בכור תריץ הכי והכי קאמר אי ס"ד יצא אחר יוצא דופן זכר קדוש בכור דכתיב רחמנא לי:
notes.en: And the last clause, which seems to you to require a firstborn in every respect, explain thus; and this is what it is saying: If it enters your mind that a male that emerged after one born by caesarean section is sanctified, why do I need “firstborn” that the Merciful One wrote?

messages.text: If it serves to exclude a case where a female emerged from the womb before it, that is derived from the phrase “that which opens any womb.” Rather, conclude from it that “firstborn” serves to exclude a case where an animal emerged from the womb after its older sibling was born by caesarean section.

notes.he: דרך רחם מפטר רחם נפקא אלא למעוטי יוצא אחר יוצא דרך דופ.ן בין אביי (לרבא) [לרבינא] ליכא מידי אלא במשמעותיה דקרא פליגי:
notes.en: For if to exclude where a female emerged before it: through the womb, that is derived from “that which opens the womb.” Rather, [it is] to exclude one that emerges after one that emerged by caesarean section. Between Abaye and Ravina there is no [practical difference]; they disagree only about the meaning of the verse. [The printed text reads “Rava,” corrected in brackets to “Ravina.”]

notes.he: אי למעוטי יצתה נקבה לפניו דרך רחם מפטר רחם נפקא:
notes.en: If to exclude where a female emerged before it through the womb, that is derived from “that which opens the womb.”

messages.text: According to Ravina, the word “firstborn” is referring to an animal that is a firstborn even in only one aspect, but as it is extraneous it serves to exclude an animal whose older sibling was born by caesarean section.

notes.dh: אלא ש"מ בכור למעוטי יצא אחר יוצא דופן
notes.he: זכר דלא קדיש דבעינן בכור לרחמים ולזכרים. אבל אי יצתה נקבה לפניו דרך דופן אפי' הכי הוי בכור אע"ג דלא הוי בכור ללידה. אלמא דבכור לדבר אחד דמחוסר דבר אחד בלבד הוי בכור:
notes.en: Rather, conclude from it: “firstborn” is to exclude one that emerged after one born by caesarean section, a male, which is not sanctified, since we require a firstborn for the womb and for males. But if a female emerged before it by caesarean section, even so it is a firstborn, even though it is not a firstborn for birth. Evidently a firstborn in one aspect, lacking only one thing, is a firstborn.

messages.text: @Ravina If it enters your mind that a firstborn in one aspect is called a firstborn and the derivation is based on the fact that the term “firstborn” is superfluous, that works out well in a case where a male emerged by caesarean section and then another male emerged through the womb. It stands to reason that it is not sanctified, as this birth is excluded by the word “firstborn,” as it is the firstborn of the womb, but it is not the firstborn of the males.
messages.quote: Actually, a firstborn in one aspect is called a firstborn

notes.he: משמע בכור ויוצא אחר יוצא דופן לא ממשמעותא אימעיט אלא מריבויא תינח היכא דיצא זכר תחלה דרך דופן והדר נפק זכר אחרינא דרך רחם דההוא אימעיט מריבויא דקרא דמסתברא דקרא אתא למעוטי דהא דבכור לרחמים הוא דאיכא לבכור לזכרים וללידה ליכא:
notes.en: If it enters your mind that a firstborn in one aspect: is the meaning of “firstborn,” and one that emerged after one born by caesarean section is excluded not by the meaning [of the word] but by its being extra: that works well where a male emerged first by caesarean section and then another male emerged through the womb; that one is excluded by the extra word of the verse, for it stands to reason that the verse comes to exclude it, since it is only a firstborn for the womb, while firstborn for males and for birth are lacking.

notes.dh: א"ל רב אחא מדיפתי לרבינא תינח
notes.he: כלומר בשלמא מאי דאמרת דהיכא דיצא זכר דרך דופן וזכר הבכור דרך רחם דלא קדיש דקא ממעטת לי' מבכור האי ניחא לי דאנן בעינן בכור לכל דבר:
notes.en: Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina: That works well. That is: granted, what you said, that where a male emerged by caesarean section and a male firstborn through the womb it is not sanctified, since you exclude it by “firstborn”: that works for me, since we require a firstborn in every respect.

messages.text: But in a case where a female emerged by caesarean section and afterward a male was born through the womb, let it be sanctified, as it is the firstborn of the males and the firstborn of the womb. One cannot derive the exclusions of both of these cases from the word “firstborn,” and yet the baraita indicates that even if a female was born first by caesarean section, the male born afterward is not considered the firstborn.

notes.dh: אלא היכא דיצתה נקבה דרך דופן
notes.he: והדר נפק זכר דרך רחם ליקדוש דהא הוי בכור לתרי מילי לרחמים ולזכרים ומריבויא דקרא לא מצית למעוטי אלא חד מסתברא דיוצא אחר יוצא דופן זכר קממעט ולא יוצא אחר יוצא דופן נקבה ואמאי קתני בברייתא סתם אפילו יוצא אחר יוצא דופן ולא פליגי בין זכר לנקבה:
notes.en: But where a female emerged by caesarean section: and then a male emerged through the womb, let it be sanctified, for it is a firstborn in two respects, for the womb and for males; and from the extra word of the verse you can exclude only one [case]. It stands to reason that it excludes one that emerged after a male born by caesarean section, and not one after a female born by caesarean section. So why does the baraita teach without qualification “even one that emerged after one born by caesarean section,” without distinguishing between male and female?

notes.he: מאי דאמרת דהיכא דיצתה נקבה דרך דופן וזכר בכור דרך רחם דליקדוש משום דהא איכא בכור לזכרים ובכור לרחמים אמאי ליקדוש (הא כתב רחמנא כל הבכור אשר יולד אלמא דבעי נמי בכור ללידה):
notes.en: But what you said, that where a female emerged by caesarean section and the male firstborn through the womb [it is not sanctified]: let it be sanctified, since it is a firstborn for males and a firstborn for the womb. [An editor’s note suggests reading: “…it is not sanctified: why? Let it be sanctified, since there is a firstborn for males and a firstborn for the womb. Rather, it is clear as Abaye.” The printed text then adds in parentheses: Why should it be sanctified? Didn’t the Merciful One write “every firstborn that is born”? Evidently it also requires a firstborn for birth.]

notes.he: (א"ל רב אחא מדיפתי לרבינא תינח היכא דיצא זכר דרך דופן וזכר דרך רחם דלא קדוש דאימעוט ליה מבכור דבכור לרחמים איכא בכור לזכר ליכא אלא איכא דיצתה נקבה דרך דופן וזכר דרך רחם בתמיהא ליקדוש דהא איכא בכור לזכר ובכור לרחמים אלא מחוורתא כדאביי):
notes.en: (Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina: That works well where a male emerged by caesarean section and a male through the womb, which is not sanctified, since it is excluded by “firstborn”: there is a firstborn for the womb, [but] no firstborn for males. But where a female emerged by caesarean section and a male through the womb, would you say so? Let it be sanctified, since there is a firstborn for males and a firstborn for the womb! Rather, it is clear as Abaye.) [This parenthesized comment is printed as a second version of the comments above.]

messages.text: Rather, it is clear that the baraita must be interpreted in accordance with the explanation of Abaye, that a firstborn in one aspect is not called a firstborn.
messages.quote: Actually, a firstborn in one aspect is not called a firstborn

notes.he: דמשמעותיה הוי בכור לכל מילי משום הכי מימעיט כולהו:
notes.en: Rather, it is clear as Abaye: that its meaning is a firstborn in every respect; therefore all of them are excluded.

notes.he: כדתריץ לעולם בכור לדבר אחד לא הוי בכור ורישא הכי [קאמר כו'] וכלל הכי גמרינן:
notes.en: Rather, it is clear as Abaye: who explained: actually, a firstborn in one aspect is not a firstborn, and the first clause is saying thus [etc.]; and so we learn the principle.

notes.he: הדרן עלך הלוקח עובר פרתו
notes.en: We will return to you, HaLoke’aḥ Ubar Parato.

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.caption: Four births through or around the womb: which aspects of “firstborn” each has, and which word of the verse excludes it.

messages.text: הדרן עלך הלוקח עובר פרתו · Hadran alakh HaLoke’aḥ Ubar Parato: we will return to you, chapter 2, “One Who Purchases the Fetus of His Cow.”
Chapter 3 · הלוקח בהמה · HaLoke’aḥ Behema: an animal bought from a gentile when it is not known whether it has already given birth.
Mishna

In the case of one who purchases a female animal from a gentile and does not know whether it had previously given birth or whether it had not previously given birth, and after the purchase the animal gave birth to a male,

notes.he: מתני' הלוקח בהמה:
notes.en: Mishna. One who purchases an animal: [the opening words of the new chapter].

messages.text: If the mother was a goat within its first year the male offspring certainly is given to the priest, as it definitely never gave birth previously. From that point forward, i.e., if the mother is older than that, its offspring’s status as a firstborn is uncertain.

notes.he: שילדה בתוך שנתה:
notes.en: A goat in its first year: that gave birth within its year.

notes.he: אותו הולד לכהן דקודם לכן לא ילדה:
notes.en: Certainly: that offspring is for the priest, since before that it had not given birth.

notes.he: ירעה ויאכל במומו לבעלים. ספק של פטר חמור מפריש טלה והוא לעצמו:
notes.en: Uncertain: it grazes and is eaten in its blemish by the owner. For an uncertain firstborn donkey, he separates a lamb, and it is his own.

notes.he: (אם) עז בת שנתה לקח וילדה בסוף שנתה:
notes.en: A goat in its first year: he bought it, and it gave birth at the end of its year.

notes.he: דבכור הוא דבתוך שנתה לא ילדה קודם השתא:
notes.en: Certainly for the priest: for it is a firstborn, since within its year it did not give birth before now.

notes.he: אם קנאה יתירה מבת שנה וילדה:
notes.en: From then on: if he bought it older than a year, and it gave birth.

notes.he: הוא אם ילדה קודם אי לא וספק הוי בכור וירעה ויאכל במומו:
notes.en: Uncertain: whether it gave birth before or not; it is an uncertain firstborn, and it grazes and is eaten in its blemish.

messages.text: If it was a ewe within its second year the male offspring certainly is given to the priest; from that point forward an offspring’s status is uncertain.

notes.dh: וכן רחל בת שתים ודאי לכהן
notes.he: דקודם אינה יולדת:
notes.en: And likewise a ewe in its second year is certainly for the priest: for before that it does not give birth.

messages.text: If it was a cow or a donkey within its third year the male offspring certainly is given to the priest; from that point forward the offspring’s status is uncertain.

notes.dh: מתני' פרה וחמור בנות שלש ודאי לכהן
notes.he: אין לפרש דיולדת תוך שתי שנים אלא דאם איתא שילדה בשנה שניה לא היתה חוזרת ויולדת בשלישית אע"ג דגדולה יולדת בכל שנה כענין שפי' רש"י בגמ' גבי גדייה דאמר יולדת אינה חוזרת ויולדת תוך שנתה ופירש בקונטרס אע"ג שהגדולות חוזרות ויולדות בתוך שנתן הקטנות היולדות אין חוזרות ויולדות בתוך שנתן אין לפרש כן דבהדיא אמרי' בריש אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כד:) גבי ואת בניהם כלו בבית אי בפחותה מבת שלש מי קילדה והתנן פרה וחמור בנות שלש ודאי לכהן ש"מ תוך שתים לא ילדה כלל:
notes.en: Mishna. A cow or a donkey in their third year is certainly for the priest: one cannot explain that it [may] give birth within two years, but that had it given birth in the second year it would not give birth again in the third, even though a grown one gives birth every year, along the lines of what Rashi explained in the Gemara regarding a young goat, where it says that one that gave birth does not give birth again within its year, and Rashi explained: although grown ones give birth again within their year, young ones that gave birth do not give birth again within their year. One cannot explain so, for it is said explicitly at the beginning of Ein Ma’amidin (Avoda Zara 24b), regarding “and their calves they shut up at home” (I Samuel 6:10): “If [it was] less than three years old, does it give birth? But didn’t we learn: A cow or a donkey in their third year is certainly for the priest?” Conclude from it that within two years it does not give birth at all.

notes.dh: ופרה וחמור בני שלשה ודאי לכהן מיכן ואילך ספק
notes.he: וספק דחמור במקום רעייה דבהמה טהורה יפריש טלה תחת זה ספק פטר חמור והוא לעצמו:
notes.en: And a cow or a donkey in their third year is certainly for the priest; from then on, uncertain. And for an uncertain donkey, in place of the grazing [that applies to] a kosher animal, he separates a lamb in place of this uncertain firstborn donkey, and it is his own.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yishmael Were an animal exempted only by giving birth to an offspring and in no other manner the halakha would be in accordance with your statement.

notes.he: ממש דבהמה נפטרה מן הבכורה היה כדבריך דעז בת שנתה ודאי לכהן וכו':
notes.en: If by offspring: by actual [offspring] alone were an animal exempted from the firstborn [obligation], it would be as you say: a goat in its first year is certainly for the priest etc.

messages.text: But the Sages said: An indication of the offspring in a small animal is a murky discharge from the womb, which indicates the animal had been pregnant, and therefore exempts subsequent births from the mitzva of the firstborn. The indication in a large animal is the emergence of an afterbirth, and the indication in a woman is a fetal sac or an afterbirth. Since these can be produced even within a year, it cannot be assumed that an animal in its first year is definitely subject to the mitzva of the firstborn.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ' שמא טנפה בתוך שנתה והוי סימן ולד ונפטרה מן הבכורה הלכך אפי' עז בת שנתה ספק היא:
notes.en: A murky discharge [tinuf]: explained in the Gemara. Perhaps it discharged within its year, which is a sign of offspring, and it was exempted from the firstborn [obligation]; therefore even a goat in its first year is uncertain.

notes.he: עור צורת הולד:
notes.en: A fetal sac [shafir]: the skin of the form of the fetus.

notes.he: בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עז.) תנן שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה באכילה כסימן ולד באשה כך סימן ולד בבהמה משמע שפשוט באשה יותר מבהמה ותימה דהכי תנן הכא בהמה כמו אשה ואית ספרים דלא גרסי התם כן אלא גרסי סימן וולד באשה סימן וולד בבהמה ורבי אומר שיש ליישב הגירסא דמשום דשפיר אינו סימן ולד בבהמה כמו באשה נקט כי האי לישנא דמ"מ שליא היא סימן ולד בבהמה כמו באשה:
notes.en: And in a large animal an afterbirth, and in a woman a fetal sac and an afterbirth: in the chapter Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 77a) we learned: An afterbirth that partly emerged is forbidden for eating; as is the sign of offspring in a woman, so is the sign of offspring in an animal. This implies that it is more obvious in a woman than in an animal; and it is puzzling, for here we learned [that] an animal is like a woman. And some books do not read so there, but read: “a sign of offspring in a woman, a sign of offspring in an animal.” And my teacher says that the reading can be reconciled: since a fetal sac is not a sign of offspring in an animal as it is in a woman, it used this wording, [to say] that in any case an afterbirth is a sign of offspring in an animal as in a woman.

notes.dh: אלא אמרו סימן ולד בבהמה דקה טינוף
notes.he: אם הפילה דם מרחמה אותו דם הוה ולד אלא שהפילה ולההיא דם קרי טינוף ובמקום ולד הוא ונפטר מן הבכורה:
notes.en: But they said: the sign of offspring in a small animal is a murky discharge: if it miscarried blood from its womb, that blood was offspring, but it miscarried; that blood is called tinuf, and it stands in place of offspring, and [the animal] is exempted from the firstborn [obligation].

notes.he: אם בהמה הפילה שיליא בלבד היינו סימן ולד דאין שיליא (מן) בלא ולד ונפטרה מן הבכורה:
notes.en: And likewise a large animal: if the animal miscarried only an afterbirth, that is a sign of offspring, for there is no afterbirth without offspring, and it is exempted from the firstborn [obligation].

notes.he: ושפיר היינו דם שבתוך השיליא ואיכא למיחש שמא טינפה בתוך שנתה ואח"כ ילדה לסוף ה' חדשים משום הכי הכל ספק אפי' בת שנתה:
notes.en: And the sign of offspring in a woman is a fetal sac and an afterbirth. And the shafir is the blood inside the afterbirth. And one must be concerned that perhaps it discharged within its year and afterward gave birth at the end of five months; therefore everything is uncertain, even one in its first year.

messages.text: Rather, this is the principle: In any case where it is known that the animal had previously given birth, the priest has nothing here. And in any case where it is known that the animal had not previously given birth, that is given to the priest. And if it is uncertain, it may be eaten in its blemished state by the owner.

notes.he: או בטינוף או בלידה אין כאן לכהן:
notes.en: Any case where it is known that it had given birth: whether by a discharge or by birth, the priest has nothing here.

notes.he: ושידוע שלא ביכרה ודאי לא בטינוף ולא בלידה:
notes.en: And where it is known that it had not given birth: certainly, neither by a discharge nor by birth.

notes.he: היינו הלוקח ואפילו בתוך שנתה:
notes.en: And if uncertain: this is the purchaser, even [if the animal is] within its year.

notes.he: ששפעה חררת דם קשה דחררה היינו נמי סימן וולד ותיקבר כדין בכור ונפטר שוב מן הבכורה:
notes.en: That discharged a hard clot of blood: for a clot too is a sign of offspring; and it is buried as the law of a firstborn, and [the animal] is thereafter exempt from the firstborn [obligation].

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that according to Rabbi Yishmael, the firstborn status of the offspring of a goat acquired from a gentile when it was more than one year old is uncertain. From that point forward, i.e., if it was bought after its first year, why is it in a state of uncertainty? One should follow the majority of animals, and as the majority of animals are impregnated and give birth within their first year, it can be assumed this animal certainly gave birth.
messages.quote: From that point forward, its offspring’s status as a firstborn is uncertain

notes.he: כלומר דאינו נאכל אלא במומו:
notes.en: And why uncertain: that is, that it is eaten only in its blemish.

notes.dh: לימא הלך אחר וכו' והא ודאי מילד אוליד
notes.he: בתוך שנתה והאי דקא ילדה השתא אחר שנתה ליהוי חולין גמורין ויאכילנו בלא מום:
notes.en: Let us say: follow etc., and it certainly gave birth within its year, and this one that it bore now, after its year, should be entirely non-sacred, and he may eat it without a blemish.

messages.text: Shall we say Rabbi Yishmael holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who says one must be concerned for the minority, i.e., he must take the minority of cases into account?

notes.he: כדקתני לקמן קטן וקטנה:
notes.en: Gemara. Rabbi Meir is concerned for the minority: as is taught below regarding a male minor and a female minor.

notes.he: דחייש למיעוט כדאמר לקמן איכא נמי מיעוט בהמה דלא ילדה בתוך שנתה הילכך הוי ספק:
notes.en: Like Rabbi Meir: who is concerned for the minority, as is said below. There is also a minority of animals that do not give birth within their year; therefore it is uncertain.

messages.text: You may even say Rabbi Yishmael holds in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis. When the Rabbis follow the majority, this is in a case of an evident majority, which is extant and can be examined.

notes.he: ר' ישמעאל כרבנן ס"ל דאזלי בתר רובא:
notes.en: You may even say: Rabbi Yishmael holds like the Rabbis, who follow the majority.

messages.text: For example, in a situation where a piece of meat is found in front of nine stores selling kosher meat and one store selling non-kosher meat, and it is not known from which store it came, it may be assumed that it came from one of the stores that sells kosher meat. And similarly, the Sanhedrin reaches its decisions by a majority vote of its judges.

notes.he: כולן מוכרות בשר שחוטה ואחת מוכרת בשר נבילה ונמצאת חתיכת בשר לשם בקרקע כשרה דכל דפריש מרובא פריש והיינו רובא דאיתיה קמן שהרי החנויות לפנינו:
notes.en: Nine stores: all of them sell meat of slaughtered animals and one sells meat of an unslaughtered carcass, and a piece of meat is found there on the ground: it is kosher, since whatever separates, separates from the majority. And this is a majority that is before us, since the stores are before us.

notes.he: כגון שנים עשר מזכין ואחד עשר מחייבין זכאי:
notes.en: And the Sanhedrin: for example, twelve acquit and eleven convict; he is acquitted.

notes.dh: ברובא דאיתיה קמן כמו תשע חנויות
notes.he: היי מצי למימר וליטעמיך מי פליג ר' מאיר התם אחרי רבים להטות כתיב (שמות כ״ג:ב׳) ומהתם ילפינן תשע חנויות בפ"ק דחולין (דף יא.):
notes.en: With an evident majority, such as nine stores: he could have said, “And according to your reasoning, does Rabbi Meir disagree there? It is written: ‘Incline after the majority’ (Exodus 23:2),” and from there we derive [the case of] nine stores, in the first chapter of Ḥullin (11a).

notes.dh: וכי אזלי בתר רובא ברובא דאיתיה לקמן כגון תשע חנויות כולן מוכרות בשר שחוטה כו'
notes.he: דכיון דאיכא ט' חנויות לקמן אמרי' כל דפריש מרובא פריש וסנהדרין דאזלי בתר רוב:
notes.en: And when they follow the majority, it is with a majority that is before us, such as nine stores, all of them selling meat of slaughtered animals etc. Since there are nine stores before us, we say: whatever separates, separates from the majority. And the Sanhedrin, who follow the majority.

messages.text: But with regard to a non-evident majority, which is based solely upon statistical information such as the assertion that most animals become pregnant and give birth within their first year, even the Rabbis do not follow the majority.

notes.he: כגון הכא דאמרת הלך אחר רוב בהמות שבכל העולם:
notes.en: A majority that is not before us: as here, where you said, follow the majority of animals in the whole world.

notes.he: (לא ילוד לקמן) [כמו רובא דבהמה] אזלי נמי בתר מיעוט דלא ילדי הילכך ספק:
notes.en: But a majority that is not before us: (not born before us) [read: such as the majority of animals], they also follow the minority that do not give birth; therefore it is uncertain.

messages.text: But the case of levirate marriage of a male minor or a female minor is dependent upon a non-evident majority, and yet the Rabbis follow the majority in their ruling.

notes.he: דלא חזינא רובא דעלמא אי הוי סריסים אי איילונית אי לא. ואפי' הכי אזלי בתר רובא:
notes.en: A male minor and a female minor, which is a majority that is not before us: for we do not see the majority of the world, whether they are eunuchs or ailonit or not; and even so they follow the majority.

messages.text: A male minor or a female minor may not perform the ritual through which a yavam frees a yevama of her levirate bonds [ḥalitza], nor enter into levirate marriage; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

@Rabbi Meir You have aptly stated that they may not perform ḥalitza, since “man,” indicating an adult male, is written in the section of the Torah addressing ḥalitza. Although an adult female is not mentioned explicitly, we juxtapose the halakha of the woman to that of the man and require that the female involved in ḥalitza must be an adult as well.

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יַחְפֹּץ הָאִישׁ לָקַחַת אֶת־יְבִמְתּוֹ וְעָלְתָה יְבִמְתּוֹ הַשַּׁעְרָה אֶל־הַזְּקֵנִים וְאָמְרָה מֵאֵן יְבָמִי לְהָקִים לְאָחִיו שֵׁם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא אָבָה יַבְּמִי׃
verse.en: But if the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, his brother’s widow shall appear before the elders in the gate and declare, “My husband’s brother refuses to establish a name in Israel for his brother; he will not perform the duty of a levir.”

notes.dh: איש כתב רחמנא ומקשינן אשה לאיש
notes.he: משמע הכא דחליצת קטנה פסולה דאורייתא כמו קטן ותימה דבמתני' בפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות קד:) בירושלמי גרסינן החולצת מן הקטן חליצתה פסולה קטנה שחלצה תחלוץ משתגדיל ואם לא חלצה חליצתה כשרה וכן יש במקצת ספרים שלנו וקאמר בגמ' זו דברי ר' מאיר דקאמר איש כתב בפרשה ומקשינן אשה לאיש משמע דמודה ר' מאיר דחליצתה כשרה דיעבד אלא לכתחלה אינה חולצת ולרבנן חולצת אפי' לכתחלה ובירושלמי נמי מוקים לה כר' מאיר וברוב ספרים שלנו גרסינן חליצתה פסולה אבל קשה דא"כ ילמדנה בהדי אינך דקתני בבבא דלעיל חרש וחרשת וקטן וליתני הכי החרש שנחלץ והחרשת שחלצה והחולצת מן הקטן וקטנה שחלצה חליצתן פסולה ועוד דמאי שנא דגבי קטנה קתני תחלוץ משתגדל וגבי קטן לא תני הכי ועוד דפשיטא כיון דחליצתה פסולה דתחלוץ משתגדיל לכן נראה דגרסי כשרה כמו בירושלמי וצ"ל דדרשא דהכא דמקשינן אשה לאיש אסמכתא בעלמא היא וטעמא משום דגזרינן אשה אטו איש אי נמי גזרינן חליצה אטו יבום וכן משמע בירושלמי דקאמר בגמרא דההיא משנה דגרסי' התם חליצתה כשרה רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי בעא קומי רבי מה בין קטן מה בין קטנה אמר ליה איש כתב בפרשה ברם הכא ונגשה יבמתו אליו לעיני הזקנים מ"מ ר' מנא אמר לה סתם רבי יצחק בריה דרבי חייא כהנא בשם ר' יוחנן דרבי מאיר היא דאמר אין חולצין ואין מיבמין את הקטנה שמא תמצא איילונית משמע דכולה חד טעמא היא ומיהו אין נראה דהא רבנן אמרי ליה יפה אמרת שאין חולצין כו' ואין מיבמין את הקטנה שמא תמצא איילונית ובירושלמי אין מזכיר כי אם טעם יבום אבל טעמא דאין חולצין אם הוא מדרבנן הוי גזירה אשה אטו איש ולמאי דגרסינן בספרים שלנו פסולה יש לפרש דלא עריב ליה בהדי חרש וחרשת וקטן משום דהנהו ככו"ע ובקטנה איכא פלוגתא והא דתנא תחלוץ משתגדיל לאשמועינן דדוקא למ"ד פסולה תחלוץ משתגדיל אבל למ"ד כשרה אפי' לכתחלה לא תחזור ותחלוץ ועוד י"ל דלמ"ד בריש כל הגט (גיטין כה.) קטן ואנפליא פסולין ואין פוסלין איצטריך לאשמועינן גבי קטנה תחלוץ לאשמועינן דחליצה פסולה ופוסלת על האחים וש"מ אינה מתייבמת:
notes.en: In brief: “Man” is written by the Merciful One, and we juxtapose woman to man: this implies here that a female minor’s ḥalitza is invalid by Torah law, like a male minor’s. This is puzzling: in the mishna in Mitzvat Ḥalitza (Yevamot 104b), the Jerusalem Talmud reads: “One who performs ḥalitza with a male minor, her ḥalitza is invalid; a female minor who performed ḥalitza performs ḥalitza again when she grows up, and if she did not, her ḥalitza is valid,” and so some of our books read; and the Gemara there says this is Rabbi Meir’s view, who says “man” is written in the section and we juxtapose woman to man. That implies Rabbi Meir concedes her ḥalitza is valid after the fact, and only ab initio she does not perform it, while for the Rabbis she performs it even ab initio; the Jerusalem Talmud too establishes it according to Rabbi Meir. Most of our books read “her ḥalitza is invalid,” but then it is difficult: [the mishna] should teach her together with the preceding clause, “a deaf man who received ḥalitza, a deaf woman who performed ḥalitza, one who performs ḥalitza with a male minor, and a female minor who performed ḥalitza: their ḥalitza is invalid”; and why does it say of a female minor “she performs ḥalitza again when she grows up” but not of a male minor; and it is obvious that if her ḥalitza is invalid she performs it again when she grows up. Therefore it seems that one reads “valid,” as in the Jerusalem Talmud, and one must say that the derivation here, juxtaposing woman to man, is a mere support, and the reason is a decree for a woman on account of a man, or alternatively a decree for ḥalitza on account of levirate marriage. So it seems from the Jerusalem Talmud on that mishna: Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yosei asked before Rabbi: what is the difference between a male minor and a female minor? He said to him: “man” is written in the section, but here, “his yevama shall approach him before the elders,” in any case. Rabbi Mana stated it without attribution; Rabbi Yitzḥak son of Rabbi Ḥiyya Kahana in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: it is Rabbi Meir, who says one does not perform ḥalitza or levirate marriage with a female minor lest she be found an ailonit; this implies it is all one reason. However, that does not seem right, for the Rabbis said to him, “You have aptly stated that one does not perform ḥalitza…,” and one does not perform levirate marriage with a female minor lest she be found an ailonit, and the Jerusalem Talmud mentions only the reason for levirate marriage; but the reason for not performing ḥalitza, if it is rabbinic, is a decree for a woman on account of a man. And according to the reading of our books, “invalid,” one may explain that it is not combined with the deaf man, deaf woman and male minor because those are according to everyone, while for a female minor there is a dispute; and it teaches “she performs ḥalitza again when she grows up” to teach that only according to the one who says it is invalid does she perform it again, but according to the one who says it is valid, she does not perform it again even ab initio. One can further say: according to the one who says at the beginning of Kol HaGet (Gittin 25a) that [the ḥalitza of] a minor and an anpalya are invalid and do not disqualify, it was needed to teach of a female minor “she performs ḥalitza” to teach that the ḥalitza is invalid but disqualifies [her for the brothers], and conclude from it that she does not enter levirate marriage. notes.he: דתנן כו' איש כתיב גבי חליצה ולא גבי יבום דכתיב אם לא יחפוץ האיש:
notes.en: For we learned etc.: “man” is written regarding ḥalitza and not regarding levirate marriage, as it is written: “And if the man does not wish” (Deuteronomy 25:7).

messages.text: But what is the reason they may not enter into levirate marriage, with regard to which the Torah’s wording does not specifically indicate adults?

In the case of a male minor I am concerned lest he is found to be a eunuch, i.e., one who is incapable of fathering children, when he grows up. Similarly, a female minor may not enter into levirate marriage lest when she grows up she is found to be a sexually underdeveloped woman [ailonit], who is incapable of bearing children.
messages.quote: what is the reason they may not enter into levirate marriage

notes.he: וא"ת למ"ד בפרק הערל (יבמות דף פ:) סימני סריס עד שיהא בכולן ניחזי אי משתין עושה כיפה וי"ל דהיכא דלא הביא סימנין עד רוב שנותיו חשיב סריס בלא סימני סריס כדאמרינן בפ' הערל (שם:) ובנדה (דף מז:) וכי לא עלו סימני סריס עד כמה עד רוב שנותיו:
notes.en: A male minor, lest he be found a eunuch: and if you say: according to the one who says in HaArel (Yevamot 80b) [that he is not a eunuch] until he has all [the signs], let us look whether, when he urinates, it forms an arch! One may answer: where he did not grow signs [of puberty] until most of his years, he is considered a eunuch even without the signs of a eunuch, as we say in HaArel (ibid.) and in Nidda (47b): “And if the signs of a eunuch did not appear, until when? Until most of his years.”

messages.text: In either case the mitzva of levirate marriage does not apply, and they would be found to have encountered a forbidden relative and entered into a forbidden relationship where no mitzva applies, as the entire purpose of levirate marriage is to have children for the brother who died childless.

notes.he: דכיון דאינה ראויה להוליד לא קרינן בהו והיה הבכור אשר תלד ופקעה מהן תורת ייבום וקיימו באיסור (בייבום) אשת אח:
notes.en: Encounter a forbidden relative: since she is not fit to bear children, we do not apply to them “and it shall be that the firstborn whom she bears” (Deuteronomy 25:6), and the law of levirate marriage lapses for them, and they remain under the prohibition of a brother’s wife.

notes.he: ונמצא פוגע בערוה ולא מיקיימא מצות יבום:
notes.en: And he is found to encounter a forbidden relative, and the mitzva of levirate marriage is not fulfilled.

messages.text: And the Rabbis hold: Follow the majority of male minors, and most male minors are not eunuchs; and likewise, follow the majority of female minors, and most female minors are not sexually underdeveloped women.
messages.quote: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir

notes.he: סברי מייבמין דזיל בתר רוב קטנים (כלל) ואף על גב דליתא קמן:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: hold that one performs levirate marriage, for follow the majority of minors, even though it is not before us.

messages.text: This indicates that the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Meir even with regard to a non-evident majority.
Rather, Rava says:
Continued on 20a: Rava concludes that Rabbi Yishmael holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for the minority.
